title: Moisture Content, Water Activity & Measurement Limits

content.overview: Moisture content and water activity answer related but different questions. Neither value is meaningful without sample identity, method context, instrument status and awareness of spatial heterogeneity.

vocabulary.definition: Amount or mass fraction of water in a material under the stated method and basis.
Measure related to the energetic availability of water for microbial and chemical processes.
Degree to which results can be meaningfully compared across methods, laboratories or times.

sections.title: The measures are not interchangeable
sections.body: A moisture-content result describes amount of water under a method; water activity describes water availability. One must not be silently converted into the other.

sections.title: Sampling can dominate interpretation
sections.body: A precise reading from a convenience sample may not represent a heterogeneous drying lot. Position, material size, equilibration and subsampling should be recorded.

sections.title: Method and instrument evidence matter
sections.body: Valid interpretation requires the named method, units, basis, calibration or verification state and applicable limitations. Laboratory quality standards support competence and consistent operation rather than blind trust in a number.

workedExamples: A low reading from a dry outer fragment does not resolve whether a denser interior or another rack remains wetter.
commonMistakes: Using water activity and moisture content as synonyms.
Omitting the measurement basis or method.
Treating instrument resolution as proof of lot representativeness.
content.practicalApplication: Create a measurement record that includes lot, location, sample condition, method, units, instrument check, result and interpretation limit.
content.summary: Product-moisture evidence is defensible only when the measure, method, sample and limitations remain linked.
